ing: thick, such as grouper or snapper, cut in big pieces
st: Mix the parsley, garlic, half of the salt and the pepper into a rough paste. Make slits in the fish and stuff with the paste.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Fry the fish for 2 minutes per side and set it aside.
Cook the chopped onion in the same oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the water, remaining salt and chili. Bring to a boil.
Add the cassava, carrots and cabbage. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Put the fish back in for the last 8 minutes of simmering, then lift out fish and vegetables onto a plate.
Measure the sauce and add water to make [[4.5 cups]]. Stir in the rice, cover tightly, and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff the rice, and serve on a big platter with the fish and vegetables on top.
Mix the butter, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, salt, pepper and lemon juice into a paste.
Pierce the lamb all over with a small knife and rub the paste deep into every cut.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Take the lamb out for 30 minutes to lose its chill.
Place the lamb in a roasting pan on a rack, add the water to the pan, and cover with foil.
Roast for 3 hours, basting every 45 minutes with the pan juices, until very tender.
Remove the foil, raise the oven to 425°F (220°C), and roast 15 minutes more until browned. The meat should read at least 145°F (63°C).
Rest for 15 minutes, then pull or slice the meat. Serve with rice or bread.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb for 8 minutes with half of the salt and the pepper.
Add the onions, tomato paste and turmeric and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in [[6 cups]] of the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots, turnips and chickpeas. Simmer 20 minutes, then add the zucchini for 10 more minutes.
Meanwhile, put the couscous in a large bowl with [[1.5 tsp]] of the salt. Pour [[2 cups]] of the water over it and rest for 10 minutes.
Rub the grains with your fingers to break up clumps. Stir in the butter.
Steam the couscous in a colander or steamer over boiling water, uncovered, for 10 minutes until hot and fluffy.
Pile the couscous on a platter, spoon the meat and vegetables on top and ladle over some broth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb for 8 minutes.
Add the onions and cook for 5 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, cumin and pepper for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and carrots and cook for 8 minutes.
Pour in the water and half of the salt. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Taste the broth and adjust salt, then bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice. It should be covered by about 1/2 inch of liquid; add water if needed.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, fluff, and serve.

ing: thinned with a little milk, as the sour milk
st: Toast the rinsed millet in a dry pot over medium heat for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and fluffy.
Stir in the butter and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, milk and sugar until smooth to make the sour milk.
Fold about half of the sour milk into the millet.
Serve warm or chilled in bowls, with the remaining sour milk poured over.
Put the tea in a teapot and add [[1 cup]] of the boiling water.
Swirl for 30 seconds, then pour off the liquid to rinse the leaves and remove bitterness.
Add most of the mint, the sage if using, and the sugar to the pot.
Pour in the remaining [[3 cups]] boiling water and steep for 5 minutes.
Pour a glass and return it to the pot two or three times to mix the sugar in.
Taste and add more sugar if you like it very sweet.
Pour from a height into small glasses to make foam, and garnish with the remaining mint.
